0001| # code
0002| 
0003| Forgel Code — thin console client for Forgel over the engine's machine-readable
0004| commands.
0005| 
0006| The client does not import the engine. Its only channel is running
0007| `forgel <command> --json` as a separate process and reading exactly one JSON
0008| object from stdout. The model, sandbox, independent QA, review and release
0009| approval stay in the engine: the client never calls a model, never reads
0010| project files and never runs checks itself.
0011| 
0012| ## Install
0013| 
0014| Forgel Code installs with one command. It needs Python 3.9 or newer with the
0015| `pip` module it ships. The same run also brings the `forgel` engine the client
0016| needs onto the machine, so one command leaves a working client-and-engine pair.
0017| 
0018| ```sh
0019| curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.2.0/install.sh | sh
0020| ```
0021| 
0022| The installer puts the client into `~/.local/share/forgel-code` and a
0023| `forgel-code` launcher into `~/.local/bin`, then adds that directory to `PATH`
0024| through one marked block in the profile your login shell reads. No virtual
0025| environment and no activation step are involved, and the same command run again
0026| replaces the installation instead of duplicating anything.
0027| 
0028| | Login shell | Profile file that receives the block |
0029| | --- | --- |
0030| | zsh | `~/.zshrc` |
0031| | bash | the first existing of `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.bash_login`, `~/.profile`; `~/.bash_profile` is created when none of them exists |
0032| | other POSIX `sh` | `~/.profile`, with a warning on stderr that names the file and the detected shell |
0033| 
0034| The login shell comes from `$SHELL`. When that is unset, empty or names a shell
0035| the installer does not handle, it reads the shell of the invoking process and
0036| then the account login shell — the macOS Directory Service entry, otherwise the
0037| passwd entry — and only then falls back to `~/.profile`. The block is never
0038| written to `~/.bashrc` alone, because a login bash shell does not read that
0039| file. A profile file that does not exist yet is created.
0040| 
0041| The block carries a `case "$PATH:"` guard and prepends the launcher directory
0042| only when it is not already there, so sourcing it again, or sourcing several
0043| profiles that carry it, leaves exactly one entry. There is no unguarded
0044| `export PATH=...` line.
0045| 
0046| After writing the block the installer checks it: it starts the detected login
0047| shell as a login interactive shell from a cleared environment, under a bounded
0048| time limit enforced without GNU `timeout`, and requires `command -v forgel-code`
0049| to resolve to the launcher it just wrote. On success it prints the detected
0050| shell, the edited profile file and the path that fresh shell resolved. If the
0051| check fails, or the shell does not answer within the limit, it exits non-zero
0052| and prints on stderr the edited profile file, the exact block it wrote, the
0053| shell it checked, the `PATH` that shell saw and what `forgel-code` resolved to,
0054| so a profile your login shell never reads is never reported as active.
0055| Re-running keeps exactly one marked block and leaves the rest of the file as it
0056| was.
0057| 
0058| ### The engine
0059| 
0060| The same run settles the engine the client runs. It first learns which engine
0061| version the configured engine source offers, without installing anything, and
0062| which version of an engine is already in place. Then it decides:
0063| 
0064| | Engine in place | Offered version | Result |
0065| | --- | --- | --- |
0066| | none | at or above the declared minimum | that version is installed |
0067| | at or above the minimum, and the offered version is not strictly newer | any | the engine is kept and nothing about it is changed |
0068| | below the offered version | supported and strictly newer | the strictly newer version replaces the engine in place |
0069| 
0070| A version equal to, or older than, the one in place is never installed. The
0071| engine versions are ordered numerically, component by component; one leading
0072| version prefix and trailing zero components do not change the comparison, and a
0073| version that cannot be ordered never counts as supported. The engine left in
0074| place always satisfies the client's declared minimum supported engine version;
0075| when that cannot be reached the run ends as a failure instead of reporting the
0076| pair as installed: the offered version is below the minimum and no suitable
0077| engine is present, the engine source cannot be read, or installing the engine
0078| fails. The failure message names the required minimum, the engine version found
0079| or offered, and what you can do next. A successful run states the engine version
0080| in place and how it was obtained: installed, kept or replaced.
0081| 
0082| ### Engine source
0083| 
0084| The engine source the run resolves against is configuration with a default, and
0085| either variable can point it elsewhere.
0086| 
0087| | Variable | Effect |
0088| | --- | --- |
0089| | `FORGEL_ENGINE_SOURCE` | engine source the run asks about and installs from (default `https://github.com/forgel-dev/forgel`) |
0090| | `FORGEL_ENGINE_INSTALLER` | the engine's own installer the run asks and delegates to (default `forgel-install` on `PATH`) |
0091| 
0092| ```sh
0093| FORGEL_ENGINE_SOURCE=https://example.test/forgel-mirror sh install.sh
0094| ```
0095| 
0096| ### Client only
0097| 
0098| ```sh
0099| curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.2.0/install.sh | sh -s -- --client-only
0100| ```
0101| 
0102| installs the client alone. That route neither queries nor installs nor changes
0103| any engine, and an engine present beforehand stays exactly as it was. The
0104| engine is then yours to supply, at the client's declared minimum supported
0105| engine version or newer, before you use the client.
0106| 
0107| The client has no dependencies and builds through the small in-tree PEP 517
0108| backend (`_build_backend.py`), so the installer never needs a package index.
0109| Editable installs are not supported: the backend implements only the
0110| `build_wheel` and `build_sdist` hooks.
0111| 
0112| ### Options
0113| 
0114| | Variable | Effect |
0115| | --- | --- |
0116| | `FORGEL_CODE_HOME` | installation prefix (default `~/.local/share/forgel-code`) |
0117| | `FORGEL_CODE_BIN` | directory of the `forgel-code` launcher (default `~/.local/bin`) |
0118| | `FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE` | shell profile that receives the `PATH` block, instead of the detected one; the uninstall cleans it too |
0119| | `FORGEL_CODE_NO_MODIFY_PATH` | set it to leave the shell profile untouched |
0120| | `FORGEL_CODE_SOURCE` | install from a local checkout instead of the network |
0121| 
0122| With `FORGEL_CODE_NO_MODIFY_PATH=1` no profile file is opened for writing, no
0123| fresh-shell check runs, the installer prints the exact line to add yourself and
0124| exits with code 0. The engine part of the run still happens.
0125| 
0126| ```sh
0127| export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
0128| ```
0129| 
0130| ```sh
0131| FORGEL_CODE_SOURCE=/path/to/code sh install.sh
0132| ```
0133| 
0134| The client runs the `forgel` engine the default installation leaves on `PATH`;
0135| use `--engine PATH` or `$FORGEL_ENGINE` to point the client at a specific
0136| binary. `forgel-code --version` prints the installed version.
0137| 
0138| ### Update
0139| 
0140| ```sh
0141| curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.2.0/install.sh | sh
0142| ```
0143| 
0144| ### Uninstall
0145| 
0146| ```sh
0147| curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.2.0/install.sh | sh -s -- --uninstall
0148| ```
0149| 
0150| The uninstall removes the client installation, the `forgel-code` launcher and
0151| the marked `PATH` block from every profile file this installer can have written:
0152| `~/.zshrc`, `~/.zprofile`, `~/.zshenv`, `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.bash_login`,
0153| `~/.profile` and `~/.bashrc`. When `FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE` names another file, the
0154| same run also removes the marked block from that exact file, so a block left
0155| behind by an install that edited a custom profile — including an install that
0156| wrote the block and then failed its fresh-shell check — does not survive. A file
0157| that is missing or carries no marker is left alone, no file is created, and the
0158| rest of each edited file is left unchanged. The uninstall installs nothing and
0159| leaves any engine in place.
0160| 
0161| Windows is not the main installation method; the fallback there is `python -m pip install --user` of the pinned revision.
0162| 
0163| ## Interactive session
0164| 
0165| Starting `forgel-code` with no arguments opens an interactive session instead of
0166| printing usage text. It shows a prompt and stays open until you leave, so you
0167| work by writing sentences rather than by translating every intent into a
0168| command.
0169| 
0170| Each sentence is handed to the engine's project agent as one free-form request
0171| and the agent's answer is shown in the session. The session also shows the
0172| project it is working on, and re-reads the task and release state from the
0173| engine on its own, so progress becomes visible without asking for a status
0174| again.
0175| 
0176| Some sentences ask the session for one specific action:
0177| 
0178| | You write | What the session asks the engine for |
0179| | --- | --- |
0180| | a plain sentence | the project agent's answer |
0181| | `plan <goal>` | a plan for the goal, shown with its tasks in plan order and their states |
0182| | `accept <task>` | accepting that task |
0183| | `rework <task> <remarks>` | sending that task back with the remarks |
0184| | `retry <task>` | retrying that task |
0185| | `pause` | pausing work |
0186| | `resume` | resuming work |
0187| | `switch to <key>` | selecting another project; every later request and every later state shown uses the new project |
0188| | `leave`, `exit`, `quit`, or the end of the input | ending the session |
0189| 
0190| A sentence that names no action, or more than one, gets a clarification and
0191| nothing is carried out. A request that becomes a plan shows its tasks in plan
0192| order, and one that becomes a task shows that task with its title and state.
0193| When an engine call fails, the session shows the reason and the next possible
0194| step and stays usable for the next request; leaving after a failure needs no
0195| restart. Replies follow the language of your message.
0196| 
0197| Adopting a repository, creating a project, setting or changing a secret and
0198| changing configuration are not part of the conversation. A sentence never
0199| carries them out; the session only points you to the explicit command for them.
0200| 
0201| Leaving ends the session at once: the client sends nothing further to the
0202| engine and keeps no transcript. Key material never reaches the screen, because
0203| a value that names a secret is replaced before it is shown.
0204| 
0205| The interactive session adds no capability of its own: every answer and every
0206| piece of state comes from the engine, and the client still calls no model, reads
0207| no project and runs no check. All commands below keep working one-shot, with the
0208| same output, exit status and `--json` form as before.
0209| 
0210| ## Commands
0211| 
0212| Every client command is a thin wrapper over an existing engine command, and
0213| the engine is always called with `--json`. `<key>` below is the project the
0214| client session selected with `forgel-code use`; while nothing is selected the
0215| client passes no `--project` and the engine keeps its own active project.
0216| 
0217| | Client command | Engine command | Purpose |
0218| | --- | --- | --- |
0219| | `forgel-code say <phrase>` | `forgel say "<phrase>"` | Turn a free phrase into a task |
0220| | `forgel-code status` | `forgel status` | State of the task and the milestone |
0221| | `forgel-code tasks` | `forgel tasks` | List tasks |
0222| | `forgel-code task <task>` | `forgel tasks` | State of one task, picked out of the engine's task list |
0223| | `forgel-code accept <task>` | `forgel task accept --task <task> [--project <key>]` | Accept a task |
0224| | `forgel-code rework <task> <remark...>` | `forgel task reject --task <task> --notes "<remark>" [--project <key>]` | Send a task back for rework with remarks |
0225| | `forgel-code resume` | `forgel resume` | Start or resume work |
0226| | `forgel-code pause` | `forgel pause` | Pause work |
0227| | `forgel-code plan "<goal>" [--milestone <key>]` | `forgel plan [<key>] --goal "<goal>"` | Decompose the milestone goal into tasks |
0228| | `forgel-code history` | `forgel history` | Short session history |
0229| | `forgel-code projects` | `forgel projects` | List projects |
0230| | `forgel-code session` | `forgel session` | Show the session the engine reports |
0231| | `forgel-code use <key>` | `forgel use <key>` | Select the active project |
0232| 
0233| `forgel-code` does not read a project itself: `task <task>` asks the engine for
0234| its task list and shows the one task you named. If that task is not in the
0235| engine's answer — or appears there more than once — the client reports it and
0236| exits with a non-zero code.
0237| 
0238| `accept` and `rework` lean on the engine's `task` command and its positional
0239| actions: accepting is `task accept`, sending back is `task reject`, and the
0240| remarks travel in the engine's `--notes`. The client adds no subcommand and no
0241| option of its own. The exact engine calls behind them are:
0242| 
0243| ```sh
0244| forgel task accept --task <task> --json
0245| forgel task reject --task <task> --notes "<remark>" --json
0246| ```
0247| 
0248| When the running engine does not provide the action a point needs, the client
0249| prints the engine's own message plus an explicit note ("no engine command for
0250| this point") and exits with a non-zero code instead of inventing behaviour.
0251| That decision is taken from the engine's return code and structured error
0252| fields, never from the wording of its message, so it does not depend on the
0253| locale.
0254| 
0255| ### Output
0256| 
0257| Without a flag a command prints human readable text. With `--json` it prints
0258| exactly one JSON object to stdout:
0259| 
0260| ```json
0261| {"command": "status", "project": "acme", "ok": true, "result": {}}
0262| ```
0263| 
0264| The `project` field is the project key actually handed to the engine, or `null`
0265| when nothing was passed. On failure — including an argument-parse error — the
0266| client exits with a non-zero code and, with `--json`, prints one JSON object
0267| with `"ok": false` and the message under `error`. A structured engine refusal
0268| (`"ok": false` in the engine's answer) is a failure even when the engine exits
0269| with code 0, and its own fields are carried through. A failure report names the
0270| engine that answered: the path configured by `--engine`, `$FORGEL_ENGINE` or
0271| `forgel` leads the message.
0272| 
0273| ### Active project
0274| 
0275| `forgel-code use <key>` hands the key to the engine and, only when the engine
0276| accepts it, makes it the active project; every project-scoped command then
0277| passes `--project <key>`. `forgel-code projects` lists what the engine knows
0278| about. Until you pick a key no `--project` argument is sent, so the engine's own
0279| active project is used. Set `FORGEL_CODE_HOME` to move the session file.
0280| 
0281| ### Timeout
0282| 
0283| The engine call is bounded. `--timeout SECONDS` sets the limit for one call,
0284| `$FORGEL_CODE_TIMEOUT` sets it for the environment, and the default is 600
0285| seconds. When the limit elapses the client kills the engine and fails with a
0286| structured error instead of blocking. The engine's stdout is always decoded as
0287| UTF-8 and the child process does not receive the client's stdin.
0288| 
0289| `--json`, `--engine` and `--timeout` are parsed as options of their own and are
0290| never substituted inside argument text, so a phrase or remark that mentions
0291| such a word reaches the engine unchanged. Put `--` before a remark that itself
0292| begins with a hyphen.
0293| 
0294| ## Tests
0295| 
0296| From a checkout the suite needs nothing but the Python standard library and no
0297| network access:
0298| 
0299| ```sh
0300| python -m unittest discover -s tests
0301| ```
0302| 
0303| That command runs the whole suite — no environment variable, marker or default
0304| option leaves a test out — and it covers the installer scenarios too, which run
0305| the real `install.sh` with a real install through `pip` into a temporary home
0306| directory and a real detected login shell.
0307| 
0308| Installing the client with its `test` extra brings the pytest the wheel
0309| declares, so a pinned revision can run the same suite too:
0310| 
0311| ```sh
0312| python3 -m pip install "https://github.com/forgel-dev/code/archive/refs/tags/v0.2.0.tar.gz[test]"
0313| python -m pytest -q
0314| ```

0001| # Changelog
0002| 
0003| All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.
0004| 
0005| The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
0006| and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).
0007| 
0008| ## [Unreleased]
0009| 
0010| ### Added
0011| 
0012| - Report the client version and the minimum supported engine version together — `forgel-code --version --json` prints one machine-readable object with the client's own version and the engine version the client supports at minimum, and it answers on a machine where no engine is installed and without contacting the network. Both values come from the client's declaration and never from an installed engine, and the human-readable `forgel-code --version` output is unchanged.
0013| 
0014| - Install the client and a supported engine in one run — the default installation no longer stops at the client. It asks the configured engine source which version it offers, without changing anything, reads the version of an engine already in place, and then decides: an absent engine is obtained, a present engine at or above the client's declared minimum is kept when the offered version is not strictly newer, and a strictly newer offered engine replaces it. An engine at or below the version in place is never installed. The finished state always satisfies the client's declared minimum supported engine version, otherwise the run fails with a message naming the required minimum, the version found or offered, and the action that supplies a satisfying engine. A successful run reports the engine version in place and whether it was installed, kept or replaced. The engine source and the engine's own installer are documented configuration with defaults, `--client-only` installs the client alone without querying or touching any engine, leaving the shell profile unchanged still performs the engine part, removing the client leaves the engine in place, and repeating the default run changes no engine that needs no change. The README documents the combined installation, the client-only installation and the engine source.
0015| 
0016| - Open an interactive session when the client starts with no arguments — `forgel-code` now shows a prompt and stays open instead of printing usage text. A sentence typed at the prompt is handed to the engine's project agent as one free-form request and the agent's answer is shown in the session. The session shows the selected project and lets the owner switch it without leaving, shows a plan as its ordered tasks with their states and a new task with its title and state, and re-reads the task and release state from the engine on its own so progress appears without asking for a status. Accepting a task, sending it back with remarks, retrying a failed task, pausing and resuming work are asked for in plain language, an ambiguous or unmatched request gets a clarification and performs nothing, a failure shows the reason and the next possible step while the session stays usable, and replies follow the language of the owner's message. Adopting a repository, creating a project, secrets and configuration stay explicit separate actions that a sentence never triggers, key material never reaches the screen, and leaving — or the end of the input — ends the session at once. The session adds no capability: every answer and every piece of state still comes from the engine, and every one-shot usage keeps its previous output, exit status and `--json` form.
0017| 
0018| ### Changed
0019| 
0020| - Speed up the suite without weakening a test — the expensive duplicated work is gone instead of a scenario: one read-only checkout copy and one prepared installation per scenario group are shared by the tests that only read them, and the bounded-check cases configure a limit below the product default.
0021| - Remove every statement of a suite completion time, duration or runtime bound from the documentation — the README `## Tests` section still says that one documented command runs the whole suite, that the installer situations are covered by a real installation into a throwaway home location with a real detected login shell, and that a run from a source checkout needs only the Python standard library and no network access, but it no longer promises how long such a run takes.
0022| 
0023| ### Removed
0024| 
0025| - Remove the automated check that read the installation instructions — no check reads a documentation file any more, because documentation is text and is accepted or returned by a person reading it. The check and the data it kept to reproduce the installation commands are gone in full, no automated check of documentation text replaces them, and every other check stays in place. The guard that used to fail the suite when a documented install, update or uninstall command carried an older tag is gone with it, so the three commands stay tied together by review of their text rather than by a check.
0026| 
0027| ### Fixed
0028| 
0029| - Refuse a free-text request to create or change key material, to change configuration and to create or scaffold a project in English and in Russian, including their bare wording — a sentence that names a key without any credential term, the configuration without the word `configuration`, or a project that is scaffolded rather than created is now recognised, refused in the session and never forwarded to the engine, and the refusal states that the action needs the explicit operation and names the client's own `forgel-code` command to use. Ordinary conversation that merely mentions a key, the configuration or a project still reaches the engine unchanged, and every refusal that already existed keeps its wording.
0030| - Mask the value of the French password label when it is written with underscores or hyphens — the label is now recognised as a secret label in its joined spellings as well as its spaced one, in any letter case, so an engine reply or error that carries it next to a value is redacted before display and before retention. Every value form already handled for the spaced label is covered, a joined label without an adjacent value leaves the message unchanged, and every other supported label in every language redacts exactly as before.
0031| - Refuse sensitive explicit actions phrased in French and Spanish as well as in English and Russian — a free-text request to create a project, to set or define a credential such as a password, a token or a key, or to change configuration or settings is recognised in all four languages the session speaks, in either word order, in ordinary inflections and with or without diacritics. The refusal-and-redirect answer speaks the language of the message, states that such an action is never carried out from a sentence, and then points at the client's own explicit command `forgel-code` together with the action it performs — creating a project, setting or defining a password, a token or a key, or changing the configuration — in the same style as the English and Russian refusals. Nothing of the refused request is sent onward, ordinary French and Spanish conversation still reaches the engine unchanged, and English and Russian results stay exactly as they were.
0032| - Mask the credential of a label followed by an ordinary descriptor word — a secret label followed by a word such as `value`, `field` or `string` used to hide that descriptor and leave the credential itself on screen and in the retained state; the descriptor now stays readable and the value, including the one behind a copula or a separator, is replaced by the existing masking placeholder. Sentences that only mention a secret word are still shown unchanged.
0033| - Remove the PATH block from the profile named by `FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE` — `--uninstall` again cleans the marked block out of the profile the override variable names, in addition to the six standard profile files, so a block left by a completed install or by an install that failed its fresh-shell check no longer survives.
0034| - Point the README install, update and uninstall commands at the current `v0.2.0` release installer — the documented commands no longer fetch the stale install script, and all three name one and the same install-script URL.

0002| # Forgel Code installer.
0003| #
0004| # One command installs the client into a per-user prefix:

0006| #   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.2.0/install.sh | sh
0007| #
0008| # The client goes into ${FORGEL_CODE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share/forgel-code}, the
0009| # ``forgel-code`` launcher into ${FORGEL_CODE_BIN:-$HOME/.local/bin}, and that
0010| # directory is put on PATH through one marked block in the profile an
0011| # interactive login session of the login shell reads. The login shell is taken
0012| # from $SHELL, then from the invoking process (ps), then from the account login
0013| # shell; a shell outside the zsh and bash families gets the block in
0014| # $HOME/.profile and a warning that names the edited file. After writing the
0015| # block the installer starts that shell as a login interactive shell from a
0016| # cleared environment, in a process group of its own, under a hard time limit.
0017| # A watchdog stops that shell once the limit elapses, and the installer times
0018| # the check itself: a shell that outlived the limit fails the installation,
0019| # whatever the ordering of its own exit and the watchdog's timeout record. The
0020| # absence of a recorded timeout at the moment the check's result arrives is
0021| # never taken as evidence that the check kept its bound. Nothing the check
0022| # started outlives it: the dedicated group, and the descendants that left it,
0023| # are stopped on every exit path. The installer then checks that
0024| # ``forgel-code`` resolves to the launcher it just wrote. Re-running replaces
0025| # the installation; running with ``--uninstall`` removes it again.
0026| #
0027| # Installing the client alone is not enough to use it, so the same run also
0028| # makes sure an engine the client supports is in place. It asks the engine's own
0029| # installer which version the configured engine source provides, without
0030| # installing anything, and reads the version of an engine that is already
0031| # present. Only then does it decide: a present engine that satisfies the
0032| # client's minimum is kept when the available version is not strictly newer, a
0033| # strictly newer available engine replaces it, and an absent engine is obtained
0034| # when the available version is supported. Anything else ends the run as a
0035| # failure that names the required minimum, the version found or offered and the
0036| # action the user can take. A successful run always states the engine version in
0037| # place and how it was obtained. ``--client-only`` installs the client alone and
0038| # touches no engine. Reading a version report, and installing a version, are the
0039| # engine installer's own jobs; this script only decides and delegates.
0040| #
0041| # Environment variables:
0042| #   FORGEL_CODE_HOME            install prefix (default: $HOME/.local/share/forgel-code)
0043| #   FORGEL_CODE_BIN             launcher directory (default: $HOME/.local/bin)
0044| #   FORGEL_CODE_SOURCE          local checkout to install from, without network
0045| #   FORGEL_CODE_TAG             repository tag when no checkout is given (default: v0.2.0)

0051| #   FORGEL_CODE_TIMEOUT         seconds the fresh-shell check may take (default: 10)
0052| #   FORGEL_ENGINE_SOURCE        engine source the engine installer resolves against
0053| #                               (default: https://github.com/forgel-dev/forgel)
0054| #   FORGEL_ENGINE_INSTALLER     the engine's own installer (default: forgel-install on PATH)
0055| #   FORGEL_ENGINE               engine binary whose version is read (default: forgel on PATH)
0056| #
0057| # The script is POSIX ``sh`` and safe to pipe into: it never reads stdin.
0058| 
0059| set -eu
0060| 
0061| # The exact markers an uninstall looks for. They are compared byte for byte.
0062| MARKER_START='# >>> forgel-code >>>'
0063| MARKER_END='# <<< forgel-code <<<'
0064| 
0065| # A profile whose last line has no final newline cannot be restored byte for
0066| # byte from the block alone: the newline that separates that line from the
0067| # block is indistinguishable from one the file always had. The installer
0068| # records the case in one comment line directly above the block and removes

0012| ## Install
0013| 
0014| Forgel Code installs with one command, and that command installs the `forgel`
0015| engine the client runs as well: one action leaves a working client-and-engine
0016| pair, with no second program to find, install or version-match. Running it
0017| exactly as shown needs no option, flag or follow-up step. It needs Python 3.9 or
0018| newer with the `pip` module it ships.
0019| 
0020| ```sh
0021| curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/forgel-dev/code/v0.2.0/install.sh | sh
0022| ```
0023| 
0024| The installer puts the client into `~/.local/share/forgel-code` and a
0025| `forgel-code` launcher into `~/.local/bin`, then adds that directory to `PATH`
0026| through one marked block in the profile your login shell reads. No virtual
0027| environment and no activation step are involved, and the same command run again
0028| replaces the installation instead of duplicating anything.
0029| 
0030| | Login shell | Profile file that receives the block |
0031| | --- | --- |
0032| | zsh | `~/.zshrc` |
0033| | bash | the first existing of `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.bash_login`, `~/.profile`; `~/.bash_profile` is created when none of them exists |
0034| | other POSIX `sh` | `~/.profile`, with a warning on stderr that names the file and the detected shell |
0035| 
0036| The login shell comes from `$SHELL`. When that is unset, empty or names a shell
0037| the installer does not handle, it reads the shell of the invoking process and
0038| then the account login shell — the macOS Directory Service entry, otherwise the
0039| passwd entry — and only then falls back to `~/.profile`. The block is never
0040| written to `~/.bashrc` alone, because a login bash shell does not read that
0041| file. A profile file that does not exist yet is created.

0024| The installer puts the client into `~/.local/share/forgel-code` and a
0025| `forgel-code` launcher into `~/.local/bin`, then adds that directory to `PATH`
0026| through one marked block in the profile your login shell reads. No virtual
0027| environment and no activation step are involved, and the same command run again
0028| replaces the installation instead of duplicating anything.
0029| 
0030| | Login shell | Profile file that receives the block |
0031| | --- | --- |
0032| | zsh | `~/.zshrc` |
0033| | bash | the first existing of `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.bash_login`, `~/.profile`; `~/.bash_profile` is created when none of them exists |
0034| | other POSIX `sh` | `~/.profile`, with a warning on stderr that names the file and the detected shell |
0035| 
0036| The login shell comes from `$SHELL`. When that is unset, empty or names a shell
0037| the installer does not handle, it reads the shell of the invoking process and
0038| then the account login shell — the macOS Directory Service entry, otherwise the
0039| passwd entry — and only then falls back to `~/.profile`. The block is never
0040| written to `~/.bashrc` alone, because a login bash shell does not read that
0041| file. A profile file that does not exist yet is created.

0014| Forgel Code installs with one command, and that command installs the `forgel`
